title: Solving Equations by Graphing
description: Solve one-variable equations with x-intercepts, adjust the graph window to find hidden solutions, and distinguish an unseen intercept from no real solution.

questions.explanation_html: Write the equation as \(4x+28=0\) and graph \(4x+28\). Its x-intercept is \((-7,0)\), so \(x=-7\). Substitution confirms \(4(-7)+9=-19\).

distractor_notes.A: Subtracts 9 but does not divide by 4.
distractor_notes.C: Adds 9 to -19 instead of subtracting it, then divides by 4.
distractor_notes.D: Drops the negative sign from the solution.

questions.difficulty_rationale: Solving this short linear equation takes two inverse operations or one graph.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: Which list contains every real solution to \(x^2+4=3x+14\)?
questions.explanation_html: Graph the difference \(x^2+4-(3x+14)\). Its intercepts have inputs -2 and 5. Both solve the original equation: \(4+4=-6+14\) and \(25+4=15+14\).

distractor_notes.A: Reverses the signs of both roots.
distractor_notes.C: Drops the negative sign from one root.
distractor_notes.D: Reports only the positive root when all real solutions are requested.

questions.difficulty_rationale: The student must combine both sides and verify the full pair of roots among similar choices.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Use x for p and graph \(2x^2-7x-4\). The intercept inputs are -0.5 and 4. The requested positive p-value is 4, which gives \(2(4)^2-7(4)=4\).

distractor_notes.A: Changes the sign of the positive root.
distractor_notes.B: Reports the negative root instead of the requested positive root.
distractor_notes.C: Changes the sign of the negative root, producing a number that does not solve the equation.

questions.difficulty_rationale: A two-sided quadratic uses a different unknown and asks for the positive root.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \(5x-175\) and widen the horizontal view until the intercept at \((35,0)\) is visible. The solution is 35; \(5(35)-175=0\).

distractor_notes.A: Changes the sign of the solution.
distractor_notes.B: Reports zero without finding an input that makes the expression zero.
distractor_notes.D: Moves 175 to the right but does not divide by 5.

questions.difficulty_rationale: Dividing 175 by 5 solves the equation directly, even with the intercept off screen.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^2+x-20\). The intercepts are \((-5,0)\) and \((4,0)\), so report 4.
questions.difficulty_rationale: The student finds both roots of a three-term quadratic and enters the greater one.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Using x for t, graph \(2x^2-8x-24\). Its intercept inputs are -2 and 6. The requested negative t-value is -2.
questions.difficulty_rationale: Moving terms and selecting the negative root add work before the numeric response.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: Which list contains every real solution to \(x^2-3x-28=0\)?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^2-3x-28\) and read both x-intercepts: \((-4,0)\) and \((7,0)\). Both inputs belong in the answer.

distractor_notes.A: Reverses the signs of both actual roots.
distractor_notes.C: Substitutes zero for the negative intercept input.
distractor_notes.D: Reports only one of the two solutions.

questions.difficulty_rationale: Several options contain a correct root, so the student must establish the full solution set.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^2-58x+165\). Widen the view to include both \((3,0)\) and \((55,0)\). The greater solution is 55; the first visible intercept is insufficient.
questions.difficulty_rationale: One root is visible in the usual graph window and the greater root lies farther right.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \((x+24)^2\) and move the view left. The bottom of the U-shaped graph is \((-24,0)\). That touch gives the single solution -24.
questions.difficulty_rationale: The square is already isolated. Setting its base to zero gives the result directly.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: How many distinct real solutions does \((x-18)^2+6=0\) have?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \((x-18)^2+6\). Its lowest point is \((18,6)\), and the curve rises on both sides. It never reaches the x-axis, so there are 0 real solutions. A square plus 6 is always positive.

distractor_notes.B: Counts the minimum point as a root even though its height is 6.
distractor_notes.C: Assumes every quadratic equation has two real solutions.
distractor_notes.D: Mistakes the minimum height for the number of solutions.

questions.difficulty_rationale: The student must use the positive minimum or the nonnegative square to establish no real solution.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the exact positive solution to \(r^2+4r=9\)?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^2+4x-9\). The positive intercept is about 1.606. Evaluate the choices in Desmos: \(-2+\sqrt{13}\) matches that input.

distractor_notes.A: Gives the negative root instead of the requested positive root.
distractor_notes.B: Changes the signs of both parts of the positive-root expression.
distractor_notes.D: Uses +2 where the matching expression has -2.

questions.difficulty_rationale: The student finds the positive root and matches the approximate graph value to an exact expression.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \(\sqrt{x+12}+\sqrt{x-4}-8\). The intercept is \((13,0)\). Checking the original equation gives \(5+3=8\).
questions.difficulty_rationale: Two radicals complicate entry and restrict the domain. The student must find and enter the intersection with 8.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: How many distinct real solutions does \((x^2-9)^2=0\) have?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \((x^2-9)^2\). It touches the x-axis at inputs -3 and 3. Count each different input once: there are 2 distinct solutions.

distractor_notes.A: Counts only crossings and misses touches.
distractor_notes.B: Finds only one of the two touches.
distractor_notes.D: Counts the same input more than once because the expression is squared.

questions.difficulty_rationale: The graph touches the axis at two points, so the student must count both as distinct solutions.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: What is the smaller solution to \(11=\lvert 3q+3 vert+2\)?
questions.explanation_html: Using x for q, graph \(\lvert 3x+3 vert-9\). Its intercept inputs are -4 and 2. Report the smaller original q-value, -4.
questions.difficulty_rationale: The two-sided absolute-value equation has two branches, and the student must enter the smaller root.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Graph \(2x^2+112-30x\). The intercepts are \((7,0)\) and \((8,0)\). Zoom in if they are difficult to distinguish; report 8.
questions.difficulty_rationale: The quadratic has two close roots, which the student must distinguish before entering the greater one.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the exact negative solution to \(z^2-6z=5\)?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^2-6x-5\). The negative intercept is about -0.742. Of the choices, \(3-\sqrt{14}\) matches that input.

distractor_notes.A: Uses -3 instead of +3 in the exact expression.
distractor_notes.C: Gives the opposite sign of the requested root.

questions.difficulty_rationale: The student must find the negative root and compare closely related exact expressions.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.stem_html: How many distinct real solutions does \(x^4+32=10x^2\) have?
questions.explanation_html: Graph \(x^4-10x^2+32\). Both low points have height 7, and the outer branches rise. The graph stays above the x-axis, so there are 0 real solutions. As a check, the expression is \((x^2-5)^2+7\).
questions.difficulty_rationale: To establish that the quartic has no real roots, the student must account for both minima or recognize the hidden square.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

questions.explanation_html: Using x for s, graph \(1+\sqrt{x+11}-x\). The graph has one x-intercept, at input 5. In the original equation, \(1+\sqrt{16}=5\).
questions.difficulty_rationale: One radical and a variable on both sides require a graph setup or a domain check after squaring.
questions.standalone_review: All givens and the requested outcome are stated in this question; no prior lesson card or partial student work is assumed.

objectives.label: Solve a quadratic equation and report the requested roots.
Solve an equation written in another unknown.
Solve equations with relevant roots outside the default graph window.
Solve or count solutions when a graph touches the x-axis.
Determine when an equation has no real solutions.
Select an exact solution from answer choices.
Solve an absolute-value equation and select the requested root.
